welcome.eyebrow: A little guidance to get started
welcome.title: Turn student thinking into your next teaching move.
welcome.body: Keep playing InvestQuest at the table. Classroom Compass helps you collect two quick reflections, see what students are thinking, and choose a short activity to try next.
welcome.primary: Show me with a sample class
welcome.time_note: Five short stops. About two minutes.
welcome.sample_note: The walkthrough uses fictional learners. Your own classes stay separate.

tour.title: Start with one useful next step
tour.body: Today brings forward something useful: resume collecting responses, open a teaching suggestion, or start a session. In this sample, a short activity is suggested from students’ reflection checks.
tour.expected_action: Navigate to the authorized sample session’s Teach view; do not create or modify records.

tour.title: Read the picture, including what is missing
tour.body: {complete} of {eligible} learners completed this check. The labels describe the reasoning shown on these questions. Missing responses are separate; they are not incorrect answers. Confidence is shown separately too.
tour.fallback_body: This card shows what learners demonstrated on a check and how many responses are still missing. Missing responses are separate, not incorrect. Confidence is shown separately too.
tour.optional_definition: “Worth another look” suggests a conversation or more practice. It is not a permanent label for a learner.

tour.title: Look at the answer and the reason
tour.body: An answer can be a guess. The selected reason helps you see how a learner reached it. Here you can inspect the response pattern behind a suggestion and add your own teaching context.
tour.tip: A possible difficulty is a starting point for follow-up. You decide what your students need.

tour.title: A teaching move you can use right away
tour.body: You get the materials, a short teacher script, a scaffold, and an extension. In your own session, choose who to teach and use the plan. After actually teaching it, select “Mark taught”, then “Check again” to gather new evidence.
tour.planned_variant: This sample already has a saved plan. Read the script here. After you actually teach an activity, “Mark taught” unlocks the follow-up choices. The tour will not mark it taught for you.
tour.taught_variant: This activity is already recorded as taught. “Check again with fresh questions” adds a new scenario; “Repeat the same questions” reuses the questions. The tour will not launch either check for you.
tour.primary: See how to set up my session

tour.title: Make it work for your classroom
tour.body: Choose a class, one learning goal, and how to collect. Use Digital for private learner links, Paper for the same questions on a sheet, or Observation only for your own notes. You can preview the questions before starting.
tour.tip: This is a preview in the sample workspace. No class or session is created by continuing the tour.

finish.title: You know the loop. Start small.
finish.body: Begin with one concept and one short check. Use the responses to choose what to teach next, then check again when it is useful.
finish.later_help: You can replay this walkthrough from “How it works”.
finish.local_note: You can explore on this computer. Digital collection from students’ devices needs classroom setup first.

first_class_checklist.title: Your first session, one step at a time

items.label: Create a class
items.body: Choose a class name, grade band, and learner count. Numbered aliases are created for you.
items.completion_rule: An owned non-demo class with at least one learner exists.

items.label: Choose a goal and set up a session
items.body: Pick one concept. Choose Digital, Paper, or Observation only, then preview the material.
items.completion_rule: A session exists for the selected owned class.

items.label: Collect a little student thinking
items.body: Open the check for devices or paper, or save an observation. You do not need to log every game turn.
items.completion_rule: An eligible saved response or observation exists in the selected session.

new_class.title: Aliases keep this simple
new_class.body: Each learner gets a numbered alias. For Digital, give each learner their own private QR/link card. No student email account is needed. Keep any name-to-alias list outside the app.

collection_mode.title: Choose the route that fits today
collection_mode.digital: Learners use their own private card links. Paper responses can also be entered into a digital session.
collection_mode.paper: Print the questions, then enter the letters learners circled in the paper grid.
collection_mode.observation_only: Record what you notice for one learner, a table group, or the class. These notes keep that scope; a group note is not an individual result.

check_phase.title: Before or after play?
check_phase.body: Choose an exit check for reflection after play. A before check uses the same questions so you can compare the learners who completed both. You can start with an exit check alone.

collect_open.title: Let the thinking come in
collect_open.body: Give learners their private links or the printed sheet. Watch completed, started, and not-started counts. Close the check when you are ready to see their thinking; you do not need to treat missing responses as incorrect.

collect_closed.title: This check is closed
collect_closed.body: You can review these results now. To collect more answers or enter paper responses, choose “Reopen the check”. The orientation will not reopen it automatically.

paper_entry.title: Enter what the learner circled
paper_entry.body: Type A–D for each answer and reason. Use a dash if the learner left it blank; leave a cell empty if you have no sheet. Device answers remain identifiable. Follow the grid’s save feedback.

evidence_labels.title: What the labels mean
evidence_labels.reasoning_shown: The expected answer and reason were shown on this check.
evidence_labels.worth_another_look: The response suggests a possible difficulty worth following up.
evidence_labels.mixed: The answer and reason give mixed or incomplete signals about understanding.
evidence_labels.unsure: The learner chose an unsure reason on this check. This is different from the optional confidence response.
evidence_labels.missing: There is no completed check to interpret yet.

before_exit.title: Compare the same learners and questions
before_exit.body: This comparison includes learners who completed both checks on identical question versions. It describes those responses, not lasting ability or proof that the game caused the change.

check_again.title: See what students show next
check_again.body: Fresh questions test another scenario. Repeating the same questions allows a matched comparison when the item versions and learners line up. Recording an activity as taught does not show that students learned it.

class_tools.title: Find the longer view
class_tools.body: From a class, use “Learner × concept” for recent evidence, a learner alias for their timeline, and “Class report” for a printable aggregate summary. “Learner cards” holds private links; “Groups & settings” holds roster tools.

no_sample_evidence.title: This sample has changed
no_sample_evidence.body: The usual example is not available in this workspace. You can keep exploring, or choose to start a fresh sample walkthrough. Your current sample will not be reset without your choice.

learner_intro.title: Let your teacher see your thinking
learner_intro.body: For each question, choose an answer and the reason that fits your thinking. It is OK to choose “I am not sure”. How sure you feel and a written explanation are optional.
learner_intro.note: Keep the existing short learner introduction. Do not show the teacher tour or teacher evidence in the learner flow.
